title: Uncorking Growth: A System Dynamics-Based Analysis of Sparkling Wine Production in the Lombardy Region
content: Protected Designations of Origin (PDOs) are a cornerstone of the European wine sector, supporting quality, identity, and reputation. However, declining consumption and global competition threaten these systems, especially in mature markets. This paper explores how institutional design, production capacity, and strategic positioning influence regional wine competitiveness. Using a qualitative approach grounded in System Dynamics (SD) methodology, this paper investigates the potential integration of the Franciacorta DOCG and the Oltrepò Pavese DOC, two prominent Italian wine appellations in northern Lombardy, into a unified system named here “Grande Franciacorta”. Findings indicate that regulatory coordination alone isn’t enough for competitiveness. Early, coordinated investments in branding and communication are crucial for self-reinforcing growth. Strong governance is essential to align actors, manage expansion, and match market positioning with territorial resources. The paper advances the policy debate on geographical indications by proposing a dynamic framework for adapting PDO systems to market shifts, with implications for regional governance and wine-sector development.
